question: Can the directly calculated noncircular deflection of measured stars and hot gas replace the phenomenological 75-125 kpc member-light broadening in raw cluster lensing?

field_equation.map_deflection: standard weak-field point-mass sum of the registered projected baryon map at distance ratio D_ls/D_s=1
field_equation.circular_subtraction: remove the curl-free circular radial monopole to avoid double counting the radial baryon profile already present in the locked scalar field
field_equation.q: one universal response multiplier; q=1 is the physical GR-strength angular baryon residual and q=0 is the locked scalar control

factorial.meaning: extent rescales component positions about their measured centroid without changing mass; q rescales only the noncircular residual

validation.zero_fit: fit q=0 geometry and source positions with six starts per system
validation.screen: at fixed q=0 geometry and sources, select the nonzero candidate with minimum equal-system unweighted source-plane heldout RMS on the two selection systems
validation.exact_selection_check: exactly refit the selected candidate on selection systems with three starts and require every image root
validation.exact_validation: exactly refit q=0 and the single selected candidate on the two different validation systems with six starts
validation.spent_disclosure: All systems and maps are spent; the split is prospective only to P0570.

cross_domain.galaxy: The circular residual is exactly zero for an isolated axisymmetric galaxy; inherit the locked fixed-RAR outer RMSE only as an angular-closure test, not a baryon-only replacement for RAR.
cross_domain.solar: The circular residual is exactly zero for a centered point mass; numerical circular-source residual is explicitly audited.

claim_limits: The map contains measured gas-shell density but incomplete stellar mass-to-light and intracluster-light information.
Subtracting the circular monopole makes this an angular closure on top of the locked scalar RAR/slip parent, not a standalone no-MOND theory.
The field is calculated in one projected lens plane and does not include line-of-sight structures.
The selection and validation systems are project-spent.
A non-unit q would be new gravitational response physics; q=1 alone is the physical baryon-deflection benchmark.
